newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberian election campaign starts in festive mood.
newsitem.headline: Liberian election campaign starts in festive mood.

text.p: Liberia began campaigning on Monday for national elections to end seven years of civil war, with three warlords and a charismatic female opponent among the main contenders for the presidency.
Supporters of the rival candidates sang and danced in the streets of the capital Monrovia, praising their leaders ahead of the July 19 polls, which will also elect a new parliament.

Charles Taylor, who launched the civil war in 1989 and now lists security as a major priority, launched his campaign in his Nimba County stronghold in the north of the country, driving there in a convoy of cars from the capital.
"Vote Taylor, the man who cares for the people above all else," read one placard.

George Boley, warlord-turned politician running for the National Democratic Party of Liberia, held a rally in Monrovia. Another warlord, Alhaji Kromah, leader of the All Liberia Coalition Party, planned rallies on Tuesday.
Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf of the recently-formed Unity Party, a former finance minister and top United Nations Development Programme official for Africa, was campaigning in Nimba County.
The civil war is estimated to have killed well over 150,000 people.

Preparations for the poll, part of a peace plan brokered by Liberia's neighbours and the Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force, have been hampered by the fact that up to half of the pre-war population have been displaced or fled abroad.
Poll organisers still have to draw up voter lists.
